verses.text: Ahaz was twenty when he became king and ruled sixteen years in Jerusalem. He failed to do what was right in the LORD's eyes, as his ancestor David had done.
He followed the ways of Israel's kings and cast metal idols for the Baals.
He burned incense in the Valley of Ben Hinnom and burned his children in the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations the LORD had driven out before Israel.
He offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.

So the LORD his God handed him over to the king of Syria. The Syrians defeated him, took many captives, and brought them to Damascus. Ahaz was also handed over to the king of Israel, who inflicted heavy losses on him.
In one day Pekah son of Remaliah killed a hundred twenty thousand brave warriors in Judah because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Zichri, a mighty warrior from Ephraim, killed the king's son Maaseiah, the palace administrator Azrikam, and Elkanah, the king's second-in-command.
The Israelites took two hundred thousand of their own relatives captive, including women, sons, and daughters. They also took a great deal of plunder and carried it to Samaria.

A prophet of the LORD named Oded was there. He went out to meet the army coming into Samaria and said, "The LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah and handed them over to you. But you killed them in a rage that has reached heaven.
Now you want to enslave the men and women of Judah and Jerusalem. Don't you have sins of your own against the LORD your God?
Listen to me. Send back the people you've taken captive from your own relatives, because the LORD's fierce anger is on you."
Some leaders of Ephraim confronted the men returning from battle: Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum, and Amasa son of Hadlai.
They told them, "You must keep the captives out of here. What you're doing will make us guilty before the LORD and add to our sins. We're already deeply guilty, and fierce anger hangs over Israel."
So the armed men handed over the captives and plunder before the leaders and the whole assembly.

The men named earlier took charge of the captives. They used the plunder to clothe everyone who had no clothes, gave them sandals, food, and drink, and put oil on them. They set the weak on donkeys and took them to their own people in Jericho, the City of Palms. Then they returned to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.
The Edomites had again attacked Judah and taken captives.

The Philistines had also invaded the towns of Judah's lowlands and southern region. They took Beth Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, and the towns of Soco, Timnah, and Gimzo with their villages, and settled there.
The LORD humbled Judah because of Ahaz, king of Israel, who had run wild in Judah and been deeply unfaithful to the LORD.
King Tilgath-pilneser of Assyria came to Ahaz and added to his troubles instead of helping him.
Ahaz took valuables from the LORD's house, the royal palace, and the officials' houses and gave them to the king of Assyria. It did him no good.
Even in his trouble, this same King Ahaz became more unfaithful to the LORD.

He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, whose people had defeated him. He said, "The gods of Syria's kings helped them. I'll sacrifice to those gods so they'll help me too." Those gods brought ruin on him and all Israel.
Ahaz gathered the vessels from God's house, cut them to pieces, and shut the doors of the LORD's house. He set up altars for himself on every corner in Jerusalem.
In every town of Judah he built high places to burn incense to other gods. This provoked the anger of the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
The rest of his deeds and how he lived, from beginning to end, are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.
Ahaz died and was buried in Jerusalem, outside the tombs of Israel's kings. His son Hezekiah became king in his place.
